t: A federation of Aragon, Catalonia, Valencia and Majorca under one king, each realm keeping its own laws, Corts and coinage.
Its fleets won Sicily in 1282, Sardinia from 1323 and Naples in 1442, building an Iberian empire in the Mediterranean.
United with Castile from 1479, it kept its separate institutions until the Nueva Planta decrees of 1707–1716.
dyk: James I the Conqueror left an account of his own reign, the Llibre dels fets, one of the earliest autobiographies by a medieval Christian king.
ev: Petronila of Aragon is betrothed to Ramon Berenguer IV of Barcelona
Alfonso II inherits Barcelona, adding Aragon in 1164
James I begins the conquest of Majorca
Peter III takes Sicily after the Sicilian Vespers
The Compromise of Caspe gives the throne to Ferdinand of Antequera
Alfonso V the Magnanimous conquers Naples
The Nueva Planta decrees abolish the laws of Aragon and Valencia

f.capital: No fixed capital: Zaragoza (coronations), Barcelona and Valencia; Naples under Alfonso V
f.founder: Alfonso II of Aragon (from the union of Petronila and Ramon Berenguer IV)
f.predecessor: Kingdom of Aragon; County of Barcelona
